environment: Figma file AbC123 node 12:345 · analyze_design.py 0.1.0 · score.py 0.1.0
figma_budget: 3 reads used (get_metadata, get_design_context, get_variable_defs). Seat: Starter/View, cap ~20 per month.

standards_extra.title: Regulatory context
standards_extra.text: Client operates in India (RPwD Act 2016; GIGW 3.0 references WCAG 2.1 AA) and serves EU customers (EN 301 549 / European Accessibility Act, WCAG 2.1 AA). Grading against WCAG 2.2 AA exceeds both; 2.2-only criteria are marked 'since 2.2' in the table.

user_story.persona: Returning customer on a mid-range Android phone with font scale at 130%
user_story.goal: pay a saved biller in under a minute

overview: NO-GO: 1 critical and 3 serious findings are open. The Confirm label measures 3.44:1 against 4.5:1 and blocks the primary path.
WCAG 2.2 Level AA (includes A) fails on 1.4.3, 2.5.8 and 3.3.2; Level A fails on 3.3.2.
One token swap (text/on-brand → text/on-brand-strong) clears 4 of the 6 accessibility findings; it is a systemic fix, not four fixes.
3 of 5 interactive controls in the header are under the 48dp Android minimum; the close icon is 20x20 with no hitSlop specified.
11 of 30 states are designed. Error, offline and largest-font-scale states are missing on the primary path.
Dark mode tokens exist but contrast was measured in light mode only, dark mode is Not Evaluated until a second extraction run.
Screen-reader output, focus order and real reflow cannot be checked from the design; the implementation audit covers them.

findings.title: Confirm button label fails contrast at 3.44:1 on the primary path
findings.criterion: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA, escalated: blocks the primary task for low-vision users

evidence.region: Confirm button, bottom of Checkout frame
evidence.required: 4.5:1 (normal text, 17px semibold is under the 18.66px bold threshold)
evidence.alt: Crop of the Confirm button showing grey label text on a light surface

findings.user_impact: Users with low vision or in bright sunlight cannot read the only control that completes payment. This is the primary path, so the task is blocked, not slowed.
findings.fix: Swap text/on-brand (#8A8A8E) for text/on-brand-strong (#3A3A3C) on the Button.Primary label style, lifts 3.44:1 to 8.9:1 on surface/page (#FFFFFF). Same swap applies to the 3 other instances listed in A11Y-001 evidence.
findings.retest: Re-run analyze_design.py on the updated node; contrast_results for node 12:402 must show ratio ≥ 4.5 in both light and dark variable modes.

findings.title: Header close icon is 20x20 with no hit area specified
findings.criterion: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA; Android 48dp minimum

evidence.alt: Header with the close icon highlighted at top right
evidence.region: see the node id under Where

findings.user_impact: Users with motor impairments, or anyone one-handed on a large phone, mis-tap the close control and land on the promo chip beside it.
findings.fix: Set IconButton frame to 48x48 with the 20px glyph centred, or specify hitSlop={{top:14,bottom:14,left:14,right:14}} in the component spec. Confirm the rendered hit area at runtime.
findings.retest: analyze_design.py target_size check on node 12:311 reports width and height ≥ 48; runtime describe frame ≥ 48dp.

findings.title: No error, offline or permission-denied state designed for the payment step
findings.criterion: Nielsen #1 Visibility of system status; WCAG SC 3.3.1 Error Identification (Level A) once built

evidence.measured: 0 of 4 failure states present (network error, server error, offline, permission denied)
evidence.alt: Figma page overview showing only the happy-path Checkout frame
evidence.region: see the node id under Where

findings.user_impact: When the payment call fails, the most common real-world failure on mobile data, the build has no designed screen to show, so engineering will improvise one that has never been reviewed.
findings.fix: Add four frames: Checkout/Error-network (retry + plain-language cause), Checkout/Error-server (no raw codes), Checkout/Offline (what still works), Checkout/Permission-denied (link to settings). Each error must identify the problem in text, not colour alone.
findings.retest: State matrix row for Checkout shows Present for the four failure states.

findings.title: 5 colour values used without a token on the Checkout frame

evidence.required: 0, every fill bound to a variable

findings.user_impact: Dark mode and any future rebrand miss these fills; users see light-mode surfaces inside dark-mode screens.
findings.fix: Bind #F2F2F7 → surface/secondary, #E5E5EA → border/default, #C7C7CC → border/subtle, #FF3B30 → status/error, rgba(0,0,0,0.4) → overlay/scrim. All five exist in the Northwind variable set.
findings.retest: analyze_design.py hardcoded_colour count for node 12:345 is 0.

findings.title: Amount field uses placeholder text as its only label
findings.criterion: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions, Level A

evidence.required: 1 visible label bound to the field
evidence.alt: Amount input showing only the placeholder '0.00' and no label above it
evidence.region: see the node id under Where

findings.user_impact: Once the user types, the only description of the field disappears. Screen-reader users hear the value with no name; sighted users lose context when correcting an error.
findings.fix: Add the TextField label variant 'Amount (INR)' above the input using text/label; keep '0.00' as placeholder. Bind the label as the accessible name in the component spec.
findings.retest: Node 12:377 has a sibling TEXT node named 'label' with non-empty characters; describe at runtime shows the field's accessible name is 'Amount (INR)'.

remarks.1.4.1: Error state uses icon + text alongside red; status chips carry text labels.

limitations: Contrast was measured in the light variable mode only; dark mode requires a second extraction run and is Not Evaluated.
Interactive-target findings are inferred from layer names and frame sizes; the rendered hit area, including any hitSlop, is confirmed only at runtime.
Screen-reader announcements, focus order, keyboard behaviour and reflow at 200% cannot be established from a design file and are Not Evaluated in this phase.
Contrast for the 2 text nodes over the hero image (lines 14 and 22 of design-context.txt) is indeterminate and needs a runtime pixel probe.

retest.verify: analyze_design.py contrast on node 12:402 ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark
State matrix shows Present for the four states
Label node present; runtime accessible name 'Amount (INR)'

cleared.title: Reading-order inversion between Subtitle and Title
cleared.reason: Verifier: the Subtitle layer is a decorative eyebrow rendered above the title by design; visual and layer order agree once the frame is read top-down. Rejected.

cleared.title: Promo chip 18x18 under target minimum
cleared.reason: Verifier: the chip is non-interactive (a status badge); interactivity was inferred from the word 'chip'. Rejected.
